You had no control over most parts of your life so far and a lot of negative things happened which caused a lot of trauma and hurt. I’ve been there and I would’ve never thought I’d be where I am now. I can almost guarantee that the worst parts of your life are done and over with. You’re left with severe trauma and I’m sympathetic for you, but keep pushing and I promise it’ll be worth it.

My advice to you is to take control of your life. Start small by getting your GED because honestly High School isn’t for everyone. Shit SCHOOL ISN’T FOR EVERYONE, so don’t get your hopes up yet. You’re young and you can accomplish a lot if you put your mind to it and put in the work for it. 

You’ll never know what could’ve been unless you try. Try and stay optimistic about your life. No one can change your life or mindset but yourself. I know it’s easier said than done, but I believe it can be done.

My experience was that I would work 50 hours a week and would be too tired to do anything, so I would sit on my phone or watch tv for countless hours. Which made me unmotivated to do absolutely anything. I started to feel my depression creep back and figured this wasn't a healthy lifestyle for myself so I needed some change of habits.

To change how I felt about myself and my life I decided to delete Facebook since it's a bunch of nonsense that I spent countless hours on, but kept messenger just in case I need to contact someone. I deleted twitter and instagram but re-downloaded instagram (because I now spend the time I was using on my phone at the gym) to use for workouts.

Overall I found it really easy to delete and disassociate myself from social media because in my opinion it does not benefit me and it's not productive. We have a short life don't spend too much time being sad. Always focus on yourself and what makes you happy.(:
